Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:

The patient, an 18-year-old male with no significant past medical history, was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of suprapubic and periumbilical pain, accompanied by nausea for one day. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical, right lower quadrant, and left upper quadrant regions. Respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood pressure were within normal limits, but complete blood count revealed leukocytosis with a left shift.

A CT exam was performed to rule out any underlying causes of the aforementioned symptoms, demonstrating a dilated and hyperenhancing retrocecal appendix containing a form of calcified materials within it. Moreover, small air collections were identified anterior to the right and left common iliac arteries, and posterior to both psoas muscles in the retroperitoneal cavity of the abdomen.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an appendectomy, during which an additional inflamed appendix, and evidence of minor perforation into the retroperitoneum were found. Surgical team continued with appendectomy in view of inferior incision area revealing no pathologic process in the retroperitoneal cavity.

The patient was monitored in the post-operative care unit and demonstrated no post-operative complications. The patient was discharged the following day in stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Instructions:

The patient is advised to take all prescribed medications and attend follow-up appointments as scheduled. Discharge instructions and the post-operative care plan have been explained to the patient in detail before being discharged.

Reply with the three characters only.
